title: User launch agents
whyItMatters: Launch agents start programs at login. Their names reveal background tools that may keep sessions or sync data running.
source: Apple launchd documentation: per-user agents live in ~/Library/LaunchAgents - https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html
notes: Names only; plists are never parsed and no launchd command is invoked. System agents under /Library/LaunchAgents are out of scope.

steps: Open System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions and note which agents belong to apps you still use.
Remove those login items there first, so macOS does not start them again.
Delete the launch agent files named in the plan, then restart the Mac.
cleanup.risk: Background helpers stop starting at login; an app that depends on one may misbehave until it is reinstalled.
cleanup.source: Apple Support, Change Login Items & Extensions settings on Mac: https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/change-login-items-extensions-settings-mtusr003/mac
